author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Lynn mother is asking the school district and its transportation contractor for answers after her 5-year-old son arrived home hours late on the first day of school. Kelly Trickett told NBC10 Boston that her son Ben, a kindergartner at Connery Elementary who has a communication disorder, could not tell the family where he was while they tried to locate his bus.

Trickett said she eventually called police because the family was unable to get clear location information. On Wednesday, she said, the bus again arrived about an hour late even though the school is roughly a mile and a half from home.

The family also raised a safety concern: Trickett said Ben was not riding in the car seat required by his individualized education program. She said he weighs less than 30 pounds. The district did not directly address that allegation in its response to the station.

Lynn Public Schools said contracted transportation vendors are expected to comply with student education plans, and that complaints are logged and followed up. The bus provider, NRT, said safe and reliable transportation is its priority and that it works with the district, but it did not explain the delays or describe any corrective action. The family says it wants clear accountability before the next ride.
dek: A mother says her 5-year-old arrived hours late and without the car seat required by his education plan; the district says vendors must follow student accommodations.
headline: Lynn family raises safety concerns after special-needs school bus delay
